Profit Ratio A : B : C = (Investment × Time) for each partner.

Investment Ratio → A : B : C = 5 : 6 : (2/3 × 6) = 5 : 6 : 4.

Profit Ratio → (5 × 12 months) : (6 × 12 months) : (4 × 6 months) = 60 : 72 : 24 = 5 : 6 : 2.

C profit = 2 units = ₹21,600 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹10,800.

Total Profit = (5 + 6 + 2) = 13 units = 13 × 10,800 = ₹140,400.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹140,400.**

Investment ratio of A and B = 5 : 6

C investment = 2/3rd of B investment

Time period for A and B = 12 months (end of year)

Time period for C = 6 months (joined after 6 months)

⇒ Profit share of B = 6x × 12 = 72x

⇒ Profit share of C = 4x × 6 = 24x

Basic Partnership Law

Sleeping Partner Concept

A partner who only invests money but does not participate in management is a sleeping partner. Active partners may sometimes take a salary before the profit is divided.

**Given:**

Investment ratio of A and B = 2 : 5

Charity deduction = 50% of total profit

A's share in remaining profit = ₹3.6 lakhs

questions.question: A is thrice as productive as C. Together they can complete a job in 22.5 days. If B joins them after they have worked for 15 days, then in how many days can they ﬁnish the rest of the job, while B alone can do the job in 15 days?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Efficiency ratio A : C = 3 : 1 → Combined efficiency (A+C) = 4 units/day.

Total Work = (A+C) efficiency × Days = 4 × 22.5 = 90 units.

B efficiency = 90 ÷ 15 = 6 units/day.

Remaining work after (A+C) work for 15 days = 90 − (4 × 15) = 30 units.

Days taken by (A+B+C) to finish = Remaining Work ÷ Total Efficiency = 30 ÷ (4 + 6) = 3 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 3 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Efficiency of A = 3 × Efficiency of C. (A+C) time = 22.5 days. B's alone time = 15 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Remaining Work = Total Work − Work Done.

 90 ÷ 22.5 = 4

⇒ Total efficiency of (A + C) = 4 units/day.

⇒ Total work = 4 × 22.5 = 90 units.

⇒ Efficiency of B = 90 ÷ 15 = 6 units/day.

⇒ Work done by A and C in 15 days = 4 × 15 = 60 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 90 − 60 = 30 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency when B joins (A + B + C) = 4 + 6 = 10 units/day.

⇒ Time taken to finish remaining work = 30 ÷ 10 = 3 days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Time Relationship

Efficiency is inversely proportional to the time taken to complete a task. If efficiency ratio is x : y, then time ratio is y : x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by each person (Efficiency × Number of days worked).

Pipes and Cisterns

The same logic applies where efficiency is the rate of filling or emptying a tank per unit of time.</p

questions.question: If A, B and C can do a job working alone in 12, 18 and 36 days respectively. They all work together for 2 day, then B quits. How many days will A and C take to ﬁnish rest of the job?

Efficiency: A = 3, B = 2, C = 1 (Combined = 6 units/day).

Work completed in 2 days = 6 × 2 = 12 units.

Remaining work = 36 − 12 = 24 units.

Time required for A and C = 24 ÷ (3 + 1) = 6 days.

questions.question: If A, B and C together do a job in 4 days, A and C together do the job in 4.5 days and B and C together do the job in 12 days, then in how many days can C alone do the job?

Efficiency of B = Eff(A+B+C) − Eff(A+C) = 9 − 8 = 1.

Efficiency of C = Eff(B+C) − Eff(B) = 3 − 1 = 2.

Time taken by C alone = 36 ÷ 2 = 18 days.

questions.question: In a class of 60 students, there are 20 girls who scored an average of 40 marks in the test. What is the average marks of the boys if the average of the class is 60 marks?

Total deficiency for 1 part of girls = 1 × −20 = −20

This deficiency must be balanced by 2 parts of boys: +20 ÷ 2 = +10 per boy part.

Average of boys = 60 + 10 = 70 marks.

**∴ The correct answer is 70 marks.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total students = 60

Average of class = 60 marks

Number of girls = 20

Average of girls = 40 marks

⇒ Average marks of boys = 2800 ÷ 40

⇒ Average marks of boys = 70 marks

**∴ The correct answer is 70 marks.**

Weighted Average Formula

The average of a combined group is given by A꜀ₒₘbᵢₙₑd = (n₁a₁ + n₂a₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is the count and a is the average.

questions.question: The average of 44 consecutive odd numbers is 144. What is the largest number?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**187**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• In a sequence of **consecutive odd numbers** or **consecutive even numbers**, the numbers form an **Arithmetic Progression (AP)** where the common difference is 2.

• The **Average** of an Arithmetic Progression is always the middle term (if the number of terms is odd) or the mean of the two middle terms (if the number of terms is even).

• For a set of **n** consecutive odd/even numbers, there is a direct shortcut formula to find the largest and smallest numbers if the average is known:
 
**Largest number = Average + (n − 1)**
 
**Smallest number = Average − (n − 1)**

• Given in the question:
 
Total numbers (**n**) = 44
 
**Average** = 144

• Applying the shortcut for the **Largest number**:
 
Largest number = 144 + (44 − 1)
 
Largest number = 144 + 43
 
Largest number = **187**

• The logic holds because the average of 44 terms lies exactly between the 22ⁿd and 23rd terms. Since the numbers are odd, and the average 144 is even, the 22ⁿd term is 143 and the 23rd term is 145. To find the 44th term, we add 2 for every step moving forward from the average position.

**Additional Information__**

• To find the **Smallest number** in this series:
 
Smallest number = Average − (n − 1)
 
Smallest number = 144 − 43 = **101**

• Verification: The average of the first and last term of an **AP** is also the average of the whole series.
 
Average = (101 + 187) ÷ 2
 
Average = 288 ÷ 2 = **144**. This confirms the calculation is correct.

• The sum of **n** consecutive odd numbers can be calculated using the formula: **Sum = Average × n**. In this case, Sum = 144 × 44 = 6336.

• The concept of **Arithmetic Progression** is vital for solving problems related to **consecutive integers**, **multiples**, and **even/odd series** efficiently.

⇒ 24x + 100 = 25x + 35

⇒ 25x − 24x = 100 − 35

⇒ x = 65

questions.question: An oil reﬁnery buys 10 barrels at Rs. 36000. There is 10% wastage. If the reﬁnery wants to earn 5% proﬁt then at what price should it sell including 8% tax on selling price? (in Rs. per barrel)

Usable quantity = 10 − 10% = 9 barrels.

Effective cost price per usable barrel = ₹36000 ÷ 9 = ₹4000.

Selling price with 5% profit = ₹4000 × 1.05 = ₹4200.

Final price with 8% tax = ₹4200 × 1.08 = ₹4536.

⇒ Cost Price per usable barrel = ₹36000 ÷ 9 = ₹4000

⇒ Target Profit = 5% of ₹4000 = (5 ÷ 100) × 4000 = ₹200

⇒ Base Selling Price (without tax) = ₹4000 + ₹200 = ₹4200

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4536.**

Wastage Impact on CP

When goods are wasted, the effective Cost Price per unit increases. Effective CP = Total CP ÷ (Initial Quantity − Wasted Quantity).

Tax on Selling Price

Tax is usually applied on the base selling price. Total SP = Base SP × (1 + Tax Rate/100).

Successive Percentage Change

If a value undergoes successive changes of x% and y%, the net effective change is given by [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

questions.question: A man’s annual income has increased by Rs. 1.2 lakhs but the tax on income that he has to pay has reduced from 12% to 10%. He now pays the same amount of tax as before. What is his increased income (in Rs. lakhs)?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of Tax Rates = 12% : 10% = 6 : 5.

As Tax Amount is constant, Income is inversely proportional to Tax Rate.

Income Ratio = 5 : 6.

Increase in ratio = 6 − 5 = 1 unit = 1.2 lakhs.

Increased Income = 6 units = 6 × 1.2 = 7.2 lakhs.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 lakhs.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial tax rate = 12%

New tax rate = 10%

Income increase = ₹ 1.2 lakhs

Tax paid before = Tax paid after

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/53f64e53bf5a6a012833c57c23e5ca50ac0e0479529655b2d398fbd6625081f0.png] 

Let the initial income be x lakhs.

Increased income = (x + 1.2) lakhs.

⇒ Tax paid initially = 12% of x = 0.12x

⇒ Tax paid now = 10% of (x + 1.2) = 0.10(x + 1.2)

Since the tax amount is the same:

⇒ 0.12x = 0.10(x + 1.2)

⇒ 12x = 10(x + 1.2)

⇒ 12x = 10x + 12

⇒ 12x − 10x = 12

⇒ 2x = 12

⇒ x = 6 lakhs

Increased income = x + 1.2 = 6 + 1.2 = 7.2 lakhs.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.2 lakhs.**

**__Additional Information__**

Inverse Variation Rule

When the product of two variables is constant (Income × Tax Rate = Total Tax), then the variables are inversely proportional to each other. If the rate decreases by a certain ratio, the income must increase by the reciprocal ratio to keep the tax same.

Percentage Change Logic

If a value is reduced by r%, to restore it to the original value, it must be increased by [r / (100 − r)] × 100%.

Taxable Income

Net Income = Gross Income − Income Tax. In this problem, we dealt with the gross income and the tax rates applied to it.

questions.question: Train A takes 1 hour more than train B to travel a distance of 720 km. Due to engine trouble speed of train B falls by one third, so it takes 3 hours more than Train A to complete the same journey. What is the speed of Train A (in km/hr)?

Speed ratio for Train B = 1 : (1 − 1/3) = 1 : 2/3 = 3 : 2

Time ratio for Train B = 2 : 3 (Inverse of speed ratio as distance is constant)

Difference in B's time = 3 − 2 = 1 unit

Actual time difference for B = (Time A + 3) − (Time A − 1) = 4 hours

∴ 1 unit = 4 hours → Original time of B = 2 × 4 = 8 hours

Time taken by Train A = 8 + 1 = 9 hours → Speed A = 720 ÷ 9 = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Distance = 720 km. Train A time = Train B time + 1 hr. After speed reduction of 1/3, New Train B time = Train A time + 3 hr.

**Formula Used:** Time = Distance ÷ Speed | Speed ∝ 1/Time (when distance is constant)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bda80b7926495bc44266bf611c762fd19b28000677446d03bde4eacabc93121c.png]

⇒ Tₐ = Tb + 1 --- (Eq. 1)

⇒ New Speed of B = Sb − (1/3)Sb = 2/3 Sb

⇒ New Time of B (Tb') = Distance ÷ (2/3 Sb) = 3/2 (Distance ÷ Sb) = 3/2 Tb

⇒ Tb' = Tₐ + 3 --- (Eq. 2)

Substitute Tₐ from Eq. 1 into Eq. 2:

⇒ 3/2 Tb = (Tb + 1) + 3

⇒ 3/2 Tb − Tb = 4

⇒ 1/2 Tb = 4

⇒ Tb = 8 hours

⇒ Tₐ = 8 + 1 = 9 hours

⇒ Speed of Train A = Distance ÷ Tₐ = 720 ÷ 9

⇒ Speed of Train A = 80 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 80 km/hr.**

Inverse Relationship of Speed and Time

questions.question: Two cars A and B travel from one city to another city, at speeds of 60 km/hr and 108 km/hr respectively. If car B takes 2 hours lesser time than car A for the journey, then what is the distance (in km) between the two cities?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Distance = (Product of Speeds ÷ Difference of Speeds) × Time Difference

D = (60 × 108 ÷ (108 − 60)) × 2

D = (6480 ÷ 48) × 2

D = 135 × 2 = 270 km

**∴ The correct answer is 270 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of Car A (SA) = 60 km/hr

Speed of Car B (SB) = 108 km/hr

Time difference (Δt) = 2 hours

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e9cce49c962048b8ea17b793e7833cb277cc6751c7ed1d7ab108ad6d4771cb96.png] 

**Ratio Method:**

⇒ Speed Ratio (A : B) = 60 : 108

⇒ Speed Ratio (A : B) = 5 : 9

⇒ Since Distance is constant, Time Ratio ∝ 1/Speed Ratio

⇒ Time Ratio (A : B) = 9 : 5

⇒ Difference in time parts = 9 − 5 = 4 units

⇒ 4 units = 2 hours

⇒ 1 unit = 2 ÷ 4 = 0.5 hours

⇒ Total time taken by Car A = 9 units = 9 × 0.5 = 4.5 hours

⇒ Distance = Speed of A × Time of A

⇒ Distance = 60 × 4.5

⇒ Distance = 270 km

**∴ The correct answer is 270 km.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Inverse Proportion of Speed and Time

When the distance is constant, speed is inversely proportional to time (S₁/S₂ = T₂/T₁).

Distance Formula for Time Difference

Distance = [ (S₁ × S₂) / |S₁ − S₂| ] × Total Time Difference (ΔT).

Unit Conversion

To convert km/hr to m/s, multiply the speed by 5/18. To convert m/s to km/hr, multiply by 18/5.</p

questions.question: B starts 4.5 minutes after A from the same point, for a place at a distance of 3.5 miles from the starting point. A on reaching the destination turns back and walks a mile where he meets B. If A’s speed is a mile in 6 minutes, then B’s speed is a mile in _______ minutes.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total distance covered by A = 3.5 + 1 = 4.5 miles.

Total time taken by A = 4.5 × 6 = 27 minutes.

Time taken by B = 27 − 4.5 = 22.5 minutes.

Distance covered by B = 3.5 − 1 = 2.5 miles.

B’s speed (minutes per mile) = 22.5 ÷ 2.5 = 9 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance to destination = 3.5 miles

A's speed = 1 mile in 6 minutes

B starts = 4.5 minutes after A

Meeting point = 1 mile before the destination

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/46e8a10baf8fdee71b873deae9fd3d37a92ea0d54fd9c3a63556e9a7ce90e176.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance × (Minutes per mile)

Pace (Minutes per mile) = Total Time ÷ Total Distance

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered by A = 3.5 (to destination) + 1 (return) = 4.5 miles

⇒ Time taken by A = 4.5 miles × 6 minutes/mile = 27 minutes

⇒ Since B starts 4.5 minutes later and meets A at that moment,

⇒ Time taken by B = Time of A − Delay = 27 − 4.5 = 22.5 minutes

⇒ Distance covered by B = Total distance − Distance A walked back

⇒ Distance covered by B = 3.5 − 1 = 2.5 miles

⇒ B’s pace = Time ÷ Distance = 22.5 ÷ 2.5

⇒ B’s pace = 9 minutes per mile

**∴ The correct answer is 9 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Meeting Point Logic

When two people travel towards each other, the time of meeting is the same for both relative to their individual start times, adjusted for any delay.

Speed and Time Relation

Pace is the reciprocal of speed. If speed is S miles/min, then pace is 1/S min/mile. Time = Distance × Pace.

Relative Speed

In this scenario, after A turns back, A and B are moving toward each other. The sum of their distances covered from that moment equals the remaining distance between them.</p

questions.question: If the compound interest received on a certain amount in the 3rd year is Rs. 12,100, what will be the compound interest (in Rs.) for the 4th year on the same amount, if rate of interest is 9%?

Compound interest for any year is (100 + R)% of the interest of the previous year.

Interest for 4th year = Interest for 3rd year × (100 + 9)%

Interest for 4th year = 12100 × 1.09 = 13189.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13189.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Compound interest for 3rd year = ₹12,100

Rate of interest (R) = 9% per annum

CI₍ₙ₊₁₎ₜₕ yₑₐᵣ = CIₙₜₕ yₑₐᵣ + (CIₙₜₕ yₑₐᵣ × R ÷ 100)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8172ff8c2c412ad4155ab124c698da80cca91ff2cad1e1169a34059e4a1f87e4.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interest on 3rd year CI = 121 × 9

⇒ Interest on 3rd year CI = 1089

⇒ 4th year CI = 3rd year CI + Interest on 3rd year CI

⇒ 4th year CI = 12100 + 1089

⇒ 4th year CI = 13189

**∴ The correct answer is ₹13189.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Consecutive Year Interest Relation

The compound interest for the (n+1)th year is equal to the compound interest of the nth year plus the interest calculated on that amount for one year: CIₙ₊₁ = CIₙ × (1 + R/100).

Difference between SI and CI for 2 years

The difference between Simple Interest and Compound Interest for a period of 2 years on Principal P at Rate R% is given by D = P × (R ÷ 100)².

Effective Interest Rate

For two successive years with interest rate R%, the effective compound interest rate over the two-year period is (R + R + (R × R) ÷ 100)%.
